roundSummary: The forward merge fixed round 1's one failure: the pull request is MERGEABLE, GitHub ran the router at the code head 793974db, and run 40921821162 settled green on every check (29 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, ci-ok success). Acceptance 1, 2 and 3 are proven, with the docs race job's measured time read from that run. The round still fails, on acceptance 5, which spec version 2 added at 19:48Z, after this head was built: internal/dispatch/pmdoc and internal/dispatch have no race jobs of their own here.

All three entries of .legion/INFRA-756/implement.json's round-2 proof array were reproduced at head 43c496a0 in this issue pod. (1) The merge claim: `gh pr view 2516 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` now answers MERGEABLE/BLOCKED where round 1 read CONFLICTING/DIRTY, and `packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2488` carries the seven-job union — dispatch-memory, dispatch-multiprocess, listener-server-change, broker-multiprocess, envoy-go-race, envoy-go-race-docs, envoy-infra-go — with zero conflict markers in the tree. (2) `PATH=/legion/scratch/tmp/yamlenv/bin:$PATH bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh` exits 0 with `envoy-go-race-docs: 755 files, 0 uncovered`, `envoy-go-race: 2072 files, 0 uncovered`, `listener-server-change: 1302 files, 0 uncovered` and `25 gates`; the `go list` package-set diff is empty, exit 0. (3) The ci-ok table: driving `.github/scripts/ci-ok.sh` with the SELECTED_BY and PULL_REQUEST_ONLY objects read out of the merged ci.yaml gives exit 0 for envoy-go-race-docs success and exit 1 for skipped and for failure. I also checked the one prose line the merge rewrote rather than taking it on trust: ci.yaml's cache paragraph now says listener-server-change builds the listener and belongs to the go-envoy family, and the workflow agrees — that job has both an actions/cache/restore and an actions/cache/save step on the `go-envoy-${{ runner.os }}-go…` key, while envoy-go-race-docs and dispatch-browser-multiprocess restore only. No field of any entry is blank.

failures.criterion: 5 (spec version 2, added 2026-10-29T19:48Z): internal/dispatch/pmdoc and internal/dispatch each run under -race in a job of their own, named envoy-go-race-pmdoc and envoy-go-race-dispatch, each with its own filter, ci-ok entries and ci_job_reads.py gate, and a -timeout sized so its measured time is at most 60% of it, stated in the body; envoy-go-race loses those two packages and the same set of tests runs in total.
failures.evidence: Not delivered at this head, as expected: the spec gained the criterion at 19:48Z, after the head was built at 17:29Z. `grep -n 'go test -race' .github/workflows/ci.yaml` at 43c496a0 returns three steps and no more — ci.yaml:2397 `go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/dispatch/api/ ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/... ./internal/dispatch/delivery/... ./internal/dispatch/store/... ./internal/bus/`, ci.yaml:2404 `./cmd/listener/ ./internal/store/ ./internal/kvwatch/...`, ci.yaml:2460 `go test -race -timeout 60m ./internal/dispatch/docs/`. There is no envoy-go-race-pmdoc job, no envoy-go-race-dispatch job, no envoy_go_race_pmdoc or envoy_go_race_dispatch filter or changes output, no entry for either in ci-ok's needs or SELECTED_BY, and no gate for either in .github/scripts/ci_job_reads.py; pmdoc is still in envoy-go-race's first step. No repository test can pin an unwritten job; the measured input the sizing needs is in the proof entry for acceptance 3 and repeated here: on this pull request's own run 40921821162, job 123625657198, `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc 1210.064s`, which is 67.2% of the 1800 s -timeout that step carries, so a pmdoc job meeting the 60% rule needs a -timeout of at least 2017 s and, with the usual rounding and headroom, 40m with a timeout-minutes above it. Two facts the implementer must have before it writes the second job, which I could not resolve here and which belong to the architect. First, `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch` is not a Go package at this head: `go list ./internal/dispatch/` answers `no Go files in …/packages/envoy/internal/dispatch`, the directory holds subdirectories only, so `go test -race ./internal/dispatch/` cannot run, the drift check has no closure to compute for it, and envoy-go-race cannot lose a package it never ran. Second, the test the spec's evidence names, TestSetAskBlockTextRefusalOfEveryBrokenBodyHoldingADecisionLeadsToAValidDecision, is nowhere in this tree (`grep -rn RefusalOfEveryBrokenBody --include='*.go' packages/envoy` finds nothing); the nearest real code is SetAskBlockText in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs (ask_block_text.go, api.go, three test files) and in internal/dispatch/api/asks.go, and the docs package already has the job this pull request adds. sjawhar/legion#2411, which the evidence cites, is titled `feat(scripts): measure Legion pull requests' merge conflicts before and after a fix` and its file list carries no packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/*.go, and no workflow run exists at the commit the evidence names (ddd6873c; `actions/runs?head_sha=ddd6873c` answers 0), so I could not read that timeout myself. So acceptance 5's first job is buildable as written and its second is not, until the architect says which package envoy-go-race-dispatch is to run.

proof.negativeControl: The same ci-ok.sh run with envoy-go-race-docs skipped while changes still selects it exits 1 with `::error::envoy-go-race-docs ended skipped, but changes selected it (needs.changes.outputs.envoy_go_race_docs is true); a selected job must succeed, and a skip here is what a failed-only re-run leaves`, and with failure it exits 1 the same way. So the new job cannot pass the one required check by being skipped.
